content: The ACCORD BP study conducted by the American Diabetes Association (ADA) investigated the effects of intensive versus standard blood pressure control in individuals with type 2 diabetes. The study aimed to compare outcomes between two groups: one targeting a systolic blood pressure (SBP) of less than 120 mmHg (intensive group) and the other targeting an SBP of less than 140 mmHg (standard group). In the intensive treatment group, the average achieved systolic blood pressure was 119 mmHg, while in the standard treatment group, it was 133 mmHg. Intensive blood pressure control was associated with a significant 41% reduction in the risk of stroke. However, there was no statistically significant reduction observed in the rates of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes. It is important to note that adverse events, including hypotension, bradycardia, and electrolyte abnormalities, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment group compared to the standard treatment group.
